Team — forwarding Acme's email (deadline Monday COB). High level asks: SBOM per model, attestation for licensing policy, and confirmation of pinning behavior. Please see my suggested bullets below and flag anything we should not commit to. I put an early draft attestation in the Drive link.

Quick notes / proposed language:
- SBOM: we can provide a CSV/Excel that maps Redwood catalog name -> upstream model artifacts (hash or upstream tag), declared license identifier, tokenizer/runtime deps (HF tokenizers x.y, SentencePiece v1.0), and any conversion tooling used. NOTE: for some upstream community models the license is "as published"; we will surface the stated license and any known provenance issues. We should not assert legal opinions about third-party license compatibility.

- Attestation: propose we state Redwood's operational policy (we do not re-license upstream weights; customers receive model artifacts according to the upstream license and Redwood's service terms). We can confirm we do not perform undisclosed modifications to upstream weights; we provide a record of any transformations (quantization, fine-tuning) and their provenance. Legal to sign.

- Pinning: Console/API flow is: create model binding -> select catalog model + version hash -> click "Pin" -> system records immutable binding. Pinned binding will continue to serve the selected artifact even if we later publish patched variants. We can create an "alert" workflow to notify customers when we release a recommended update; no automatic roll-forward unless the customer toggles opt-in. Karthik/Hannah: confirm we can include a screenshot of the console pinning UI in the RFP appendix.

Ask: Neha — can you review the attestation draft for any language that might be construed as legal guarantee vs. operational description? Karthik — can you produce a short one-page diagram of the pinning / update flow and confirm UI copy we can include? Hannah — any provenance details about conversion/quantization we should explicitly call out?

Thanks —
Aisha

Tom —

Attached is the final attestation (signed by our Head of Legal) and the SBOM extract you requested. Highlights and clarifications for Acme legal team:

- SBOM contents: for each catalog model we provide: Redwood catalog name, upstream model id (and checksum where available), declared license identifier (SPDX tag where published), tokenizer/runtime components (with versions), and notes on any conversion (e.g., FP32 -> 4-bit quant). Items marked "provenance-note" indicate where upstream source metadata was incomplete.

- Licensing attestation: we state facts about our process and do NOT provide legal opinions about third-party license compatibility. The attestation confirms that Redwood does not re-license upstream model weights; customers access model artifacts via Redwood's serving endpoint subject to the upstream license and Redwood's Customer Terms. Where we provide model derivatives (e.g., quantized artifacts), we include transformation logs and a manifest describing the change.

- Pinning & updates: the Console "Pin model version" feature creates an immutable binding. We will never auto-roll a pinned binding. We will send notification emails and surface a "Recommended update" flag in the Console when a newer variant is available; customers accept updates via a discrete action. For Dedicated/Private deployments, we also document the patch process in the onboarding playbook.
